steps.what: Observe mechanical problems and describe symptoms and vehicle identity
Report mechanical problems and clarify urgent concerns with the maintenance contact

tasks.design: Keep observation and reporting with the driver through the existing fleet fault channel {OTHER}. No diagnostic model or new automatic fault classification is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful reports require first-hand observations and clear communication of urgency.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing fleet reporting channels already support this exchange.
tasks.still_hard: Describe intermittent symptoms without pretending to diagnose the vehicle.
tasks.human_edge: Notice abnormal behaviour and explain its circumstances.
tasks.altitude: Reliable first-hand reporting remains the task.

evidence.claim: Fault observation and reporting retain human time in this unchanged design.

assumptions: The boundary ends at reporting, before diagnosis and repair.
The driver produces symptoms, circumstances and vehicle identity in s1; capture and clarification remain fully counted.
No free structured fault code or sensor diagnosis is assumed.
Existing channels suffice; no new upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Current reporting channel and duplicated entry
research_questions: How often must drivers repeat a report across channels?

already_counted.description: Observation and report clarification remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No changed system or new upkeep.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 and R=100; zero gross or net saving. No duplicate-entry baseline is assumed.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Inspect inventory loads and record observed item identifiers, quantities and units
Compare observed inventory quantities with shipping papers and identify differences
Resolve load discrepancies with the shipper and confirm the checked load record

tasks.design: Configure a comparison view in the existing transport system {OTHER}. It matches captured quantities to the shipper manifest while the driver retains physical inspection, review and discrepancy resolution.
tasks.previous_blocker: Manual row matching repeats clerical work but a manifest cannot prove physical contents.
tasks.enabler_now: Electronic consignment notes are available; matching observations requires a separate native configuration.
tasks.still_hard: Count mixed goods and interpret units and substitutions.
tasks.human_edge: Establish what is physically loaded and resolve disagreements.
tasks.altitude: Reduce row matching while preserving the physical check.

reach.learn: Which packing records support reliable checks

evidence.claim: TransFollow eCMR in Qargo creates, issues and signs consignment notes inside the TMS.
Native comparison of captured observations is proposed configuration, not demonstrated physical verification.

assumptions: The shipper produces shipment identifiers, item identifiers, quantities and units during existing dispatch preparation; that unchanged capture is outside this driver task.
The driver produces observed item identifiers, quantities and units in s1; all capture stays in its unchanged 70 percent share.
Missing identifiers, incompatible units, paper manifests or offline conditions require manual comparison with no saving.
Configure the current transport system first; deploy only if capture fits the retained s1 time.
No load is deemed correct from the manifest alone; review and discrepancy discussion remain.
research_questions: Does native matching save time after observation capture and corrections?

already_counted.description: Inspection, capture and discrepancy handling remain in full.

incremental.description: Driver feedback on erroneous item mappings.
Transport administrator maintains item and unit mappings.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1: B=100, R=70+7.5+15=92.5; gross 7.5 less 1 focal upkeep gives net 6.5. Low covers manual fallback or capture overhead consuming the gain. Physical checking has no reduction.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Read maps and follow geographic directions

steps.what: Read written directions and clarify the destination and access instructions
Read maps and follow geographic directions while checking road signs and access

tasks.design: Continue using existing maps and navigation {OTHER}, with the driver interpreting directions and access. No new routing service or autonomous driving function is introduced.
tasks.previous_blocker: Directions may omit an entrance or conflict with conditions.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing navigation already assists map reading; its benefit belongs to the baseline.
tasks.still_hard: Resolve ambiguous destinations and unsuitable approaches.
tasks.human_edge: Relate instructions to actual road conditions and delivery entrances.

evidence.claim: Existing navigation retains driver interpretation of destinations and access.

assumptions: Dispatch supplies the address and written instructions from existing order intake; the customer supplies access information.
Driver clarification and destination entry are retained in s1; no free structured address or geocoding is assumed.
Actual driving is outside this reading task; current navigation is already in the baseline.
No changed system or new upkeep is introduced.
research_questions: How often do written directions identify the wrong entrance?

already_counted.description: Clarification and interpretation remain fully counted.

incremental.description: No new routing service or maintenance.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work yield zero new saving. Navigation already exists in the baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Present bills and receipts and collect payments

steps.what: Check bills against delivered goods and confirm the amount due
Present bills and receipts and collect payments from the customer
Record collected payments and identify unpaid balances for the office

tasks.design: Keep collection in the existing billing and payment tools {OTHER}. Without evidence of duplicate driver entry, this design claims no new saving from receipts or terminals already used.
tasks.previous_blocker: The driver must verify the bill, handle the exchange and account for money.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing billing and payment channels support this task.
tasks.still_hard: Handle disputed quantities and failed payments.
tasks.human_edge: Explain the bill and address the immediate customer concern.
tasks.altitude: Maintain a clear payment exchange and accurate office handoff.

reach.task: Resolve unpaid balances from the payment record

evidence.claim: The Qargo case reports faster invoice issuance rather than measured driver payment-collection savings.
No new saving is estimated without evidence of removable duplicate driver entry.

assumptions: Accounts produces the issued bill during existing billing; the driver produces the delivery record during the separate delivery task.
Bill checking, customer handling and payment capture are fully retained in s1-s3.
No free structured payment event or new terminal feed is assumed.
Billing creation and office reconciliation remain outside this collection task; no new upkeep is introduced.
unknowns: Payment methods and existing receipt automation
research_questions: Is duplicate driver payment entry material beyond the retained record?

already_counted.description: Bill checking, collection and payment recording remain fully counted.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and zero incremental work yield zero saving. Faster office invoicing is not driver labour saved.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Retain driver responsibility for physical verification, route interpretation and customer exchanges.
reach: Explain load discrepancies to stock staff
Provide accounts with clear payment exceptions
